evidence: objc2-web-kit WKContentWorld, WKUserScript, and content-world-scoped WKScriptMessageHandler APIs
capabilities.limitations: No agent runtime is installed in a product context yet. The M1 adapter installs one immutable diagnostic runtime at document end, accepts only closed query rows, emits bounded one-way typed messages, and loads a fresh document for every row. Public evaluateJavaScript and callAsyncJavaScript are rejected because current WebKit invokes both with a forced user gesture; private no-user-gesture SPI is prohibited.
The adapter can route directly to its owned WKWebView without moving the system pointer. Hidden/background trust, effect, and no-focus-theft behavior remain pending named-device execution.

The adapter calls the owned AppKit accessibility element directly and does not use cross-process AXUIElement authority. Apple's Boolean reports dispatch only, so the fixed fixture independently verifies the page effect.
The current probe does not post global pointer or keyboard events. Adding and running this baseline requires explicit operator authorization and visible foreground control.

Pinned Wry exposes its WRY_WEBVIEW container, whose window procedure identifies the first direct child as the WebView document for focus. The adapter revalidates that owned child's container/first-child/parent/thread/process/input-locale identity before and after every fixed bounded SendMessageTimeoutW mouse/key step, and receiver destruction fails dispatch. Key and character messages use target-layout MapVirtualKeyExW extended scan-code mapping and preserve the Win32 extended-key and up-transition flags. Hidden/background admission rejects host foreground/activation or owned-subtree keyboard focus before the first row, rather than accepting a stolen baseline. It verifies exact navigation identity, an ephemeral UDF plus InPrivate postcondition, and two-factor process exit before deletion. Cross-compilation does not prove hidden/background trusted input, effect coverage, or no focus theft.

Only hidden owned contexts with exact Suspend capability and no other native work are admitted. An atomic fixed-deadline owner retains late TrySuspend callback reconciliation after timeout or cancellation; final state is recorded only after hidden-owner attestation and IsSuspended readback. Resource audit and content-policy replacement fail closed while state is ambiguous. A release-excluded suspension mode within the six-mode Windows semantic/lifecycle cohort and offline reviewer is implemented but has no physical result. Cross-compilation does not prove physical suspend/resume behavior, memory reduction, long-running-script timing, renderer-loss races, or resource savings.

WebView2 exposes URI, NavigationId, and IsRedirected together and preserves one NavigationId across redirects. Zephium admits only an explicit bounded origin scope, requires exact native identity and at most eight redirect events, and settles the authoritative final committed URL. This is an acceptance and settlement boundary, not proof of zero network contact: Microsoft notes that the GET may already be in progress while NavigationStarting is handled. The release-excluded fixed loop/chain mode is prepared but has no physical result.

The supported WKNavigation callback surface preserves native identity but does not provide an authoritative intermediate destination URL. Pinned Wry therefore reports the registered initial URL for redirect events and samples WKWebView.URL at commit. Zephium combines the synchronous static URL policy with exact native identity, an eight-hop ceiling, and final-commit validation. No physical redirect run has occurred.

The pinned public WKWebView surface has no proven equivalent to WebView2 TrySuspend plus IsSuspended readback. Hiding a view or relying on process policy is not reported as a settled suspend transition.

Composition-controller input cannot be generalized to Zephium's ordinary HWND controller. Adopting it would change rendering/ownership integration and requires a separate evidence-backed design decision.

The adapter accepts only a closed three-variant CDP method enum and serializes one Input.dispatchMouseEvent or Input.dispatchKeyEvent completion at a time. Fixed Runtime.evaluate observation sets userGesture false; a raw COM completion bounds UTF-16 and UTF-8 before allocation and accepts bounded by-value strings only. Physical Windows behavior remains unqualified; CDP cannot enter domain or model contracts.
